text: When the two men recognized each other, they shook hands warmly, deeply moved to meet again in such different times. <break time="0.8s" /> What times we live in, sighed Monsieur Sauvage, and Morissot answered that at least it was the first fine day of the year. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking on side by side, Morissot said sadly, And the fishing, What good memories, and Sauvage asked, When shall we go back. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon they went into a small café for a glass of absinthe, and after a second glass in another café, they came out feeling dizzy. <break time="0.8s" /> The day was mild with a gentle breeze, and Sauvage, who felt even dizzier in the warm air, suddenly stopped in the street. <break time="0.8s" /> Shall we go there, he asked, and when Morissot asked where, he said, Fishing, of course, on our island. <break time="0.8s" /> The French outposts are near Colombes, and I know Colonel Dumoulin, so they will easily let us pass, Sauvage explained. <break time="0.8s" /> Trembling with desire, Morissot agreed at once, and an hour later the two friends, carrying their fishing gear, were walking along the highway. <break time="0.8s" /> The colonel smiled at their strange wish, but he gave them a pass, and with it they set off again toward the river.
